item.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act
item.description: The warnings surfaced in a trove of unreported court records. "I have been fighting about fixing this for months with people who didn't think the harms are severe enough," wrote one executive.

item.title: In Dublin, tech workers raise concerns about AI
item.description: Dublin, Ireland, is a longtime hub for American tech companies. A group of workers held a summit to discuss their concerns about AI in Irish workplaces and life.

item.description: AI models are transforming hurricane forecasting. They provided some of the most accurate predictions of the track of Hurricane Isaias.

item.title: At SF Tech Week, a vibe check on how people in Silicon Valley feel about the AI boom
item.description: In Silicon Valley, the AI boom means a lot of people are excited about this new technology, but concerned about when the music might stop. NPR went to San Francisco Tech Week to take the pulse.

item.title: To train robots, AI companies are paying people in India to film themselves doing chores
item.description: Men and women across India are being paid to record themselves doing domestic jobs as developers train AI robots to do household chores.

item.title: Inside the race between Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos for control of outer space
item.description: The Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel says Musk and Bezos each want to colonize the moon, mine its resources and launch thousands more satellites. He says their only real competition is each other.
